rv.q: This is an essential revival; that Childress’s work is finally being seen is, at least, one injustice corrected.

Yet as Moodie literally moves the stage with her bare hands in the final moments, as Childress raises questions about representation that startle with their modernity, an uneven evening becomes an unforgettable one.

This is not quite the scorching evening it might be – Nancy Medina's production sometimes moves rather too stiffly – but Tanya Moodie is impressive throughout: a never-flinching force who comes to glory in the play's closing sequence.
Trouble in Mind, National’s Dorfman Theatre, review: a timely – yet uneven.

Studying systematic racism through the prism of a witty, well observed backstage comedy drama, this is a play that celebrates theatricality while attacking the troublesome tropes that went unexamined for generations within the industry, and in the world at large.
Trouble in Mind is an engaging and stirring piece of activist theatre which wrestles with the structural problems and racial inequalities at the heart of show business.
This revival is a timely reminder.
This revival of an American classic, complete with its moments of trouble, is both relevant and fun.

cn.t: Critics praise Alice Childress's 1955 play as funny, startling, and remarkably modern, with a rare sting in its depiction of racism in theater that remains powerfully relevant today.
